title: Catalogue with opaque cursor pagination
prompt: Build an in-memory HTTP catalogue. POST /items accepts exactly name (nonempty string of at most 80 characters) and price (integer >= 0) and returns 201 {id,name,price}, where id is an integer starting at 1 and increasing by 1 in creation order. Invalid or malformed input returns 400. GET /items returns 200 {items,next_cursor}. Query parameters: sort is name or price (default name); dir is asc or desc (default asc); limit is an integer 1..50 (default 10); cursor is an opaque string taken from a previous next_cursor. Items are ordered by the sort field (names compared in plain code-unit string order, prices numerically), reversed when dir is desc, with ties always broken by id ascending regardless of dir. Pages use keyset semantics: a request with a cursor returns the next items strictly after the position of the last item of the previous page in that ordering, so items created between page requests never cause duplicates or shifts, and an item created at an earlier position is not returned. next_cursor is null when no items remain after the page and is never returned for an empty remainder. A cursor used with a different sort or dir than it was issued for, a malformed or forged cursor, an unknown query parameter and invalid sort, dir or limit values return 400. No persistence or external services are needed.
